text:
maria: FYI rolled out shim-warmup heuristic to canary pool at 04:12 UTC. Immediately saw a p95 bump and a small throughput dip. Anyone else seeing this?

jake: saw the spike on the dashboard. p95 +14ms for ~10m, throughput down ~6%. link: https://graf.redwood/p/cluster-gg4/latency (canary)

sophia: grabbing traces now. can you paste a few example request shapes?

maria: mostly short responses (<= 48 tokens) + some 128-token tails. root log snippet: ```
batcher: event=window_shim_merge waited_ms=18 tokens_merged=9 origin=continuous-batcher
kernel-router: selected=small_batch_kernel reason=shape_hint
```

perf-bot: :warning: SLA alert: cluster-gg4 latency p95 exceeded target (1.2s -> 1.214s) for 6m

jake: initial hypothesis: shim-warmup encourages earlier merges which increases small-batch kernel usage. small_batch_kernel has higher per-token overhead on this model/hardware combo.

sophia: ran a lightweight perf sample against canary: 
- small_batch_kernel: 1.9ms/token (median)
- default_kernel: 1.2ms/token (median)
- avg batch wait in queue: 12ms -> 30ms during the spike

maria: interesting — also KV cache miss rate nudged up ~3ppt during the window. logs show more prefetch attempts and a few evictions. could be cache churn from earlier merges.

jake: so two compounding effects: more small-kernel calls (higher compute cost) + slightly higher KV miss/prefetch stalls. explains p95 and throughput drop.

sophia: grabbing a flame graph now, but early look shows time in batcher.dequeue and kernel-init increased.

maria: can we try reverting shim-warmup only on the canary pool? I'll patch config to disable "shim_warmup": true -> false for canary flag.

jake: +1 roll back on canary first. also propose reducing token_budget_target 64 -> 48 as a safety to avoid over-merge.

sophia: quick rollback command: ```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/config \
  -d '{"cluster":"canary-gg4","continuous_batching": {"shim_warmup": false, "token_budget_target": 48}}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```

perf-bot: action: config-change applied to canary-gg4 by maria at 04:28 UTC

maria: applied rollback at 04:28. metrics starting to show improvement.

jake: after ~3m p95 back to baseline, throughput restored. can we mark this mitigated and schedule follow-up?

sophia: saving flame graphs and kernel histograms to /tmp/gg4-shim-warmup-219874. I see kernel routing histogram: small_kernel usage went from 8% -> 23% during rollout.

maria: opened follow-up ticket INF-7843 with traces, flame, and config diffs. https://issues.redwood/INF-7843

jake: follow-ups we should do: (1) perf sweep of small_batch_kernel on GG4 HW with representative prompt mixes, (2) add a circuit-breaker to avoid >15% small_kernel routing change in 1m, (3) KV cache eviction instrumentation per-prefix.

sophia: also want an A/B that keeps shim_warmup but forces kernel_affinity=off to isolate kernel selection effect.

maria: agreed. for now canary rollback is good. i'll leave the feature gated until we run perf sweep. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: incident resolved for cluster-gg4 at 04:33 UTC

jake: will draft a short blameless postmortem and add proposed checkpoints to the rollout checklist (kernel histograms, kv churn monitor, rollback playbook).

sophia: scheduling perf tests for tomorrow 01:00 UTC. i'll post results in this thread.

maria: closing on monitoring side — adding an automated alert when kernel routing delta > 10% over 5m.

jake: nice. moving to follow-up column.

sophia: thanks, logging off.

maria: night all.
